clue.text: Run skinhead accommodation with some hesitation

indicators.note: the head of the word skin is its opening letter, signalled by skinhead split in two

parts.note: a camp is temporary accommodation, as in tents or huts
er is the sound of someone hesitating in speech

explanation.surface: A shaven-headed lodger hesitantly makes a dash for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' looks like the youth subculture; split it into 'skin' + 'head' and take S.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to dash about quickly, a lively kind of running.

clue.text: Have misgivings about lightweight

definitions.meaning: an old apothecaries' unit of weight, twenty grains

explanation.surface: Doubts about a boxer in a lower weight class.
explanation.definitionFit: To scruple is to hesitate from conscience, and it was also a small apothecaries' weight.

clue.text: A large number come to 'religious centre for confession

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals
a mission is a church centre for missionary work

explanation.surface: Crowds turn up at a church to own up to their sins.
explanation.definitionFit: An admission is an acknowledgement of guilt or fault.

clue.text: Page with a keen desire to chuck it!

parts.note: an itch is a restless longing

explanation.surface: A frustrated page-boy longs to throw in the towel.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch something is to throw or toss it.

clue.text: Defying rates isn't fashionable

indicators.note: something fashioned is shaped anew, so these letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A protest against local taxes being out of vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' is read as 'able to be fashioned', signalling the anagram of RATES ISNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistant means opposing or withstanding, close to defiant.

clue.text: Pointed to copperhead about to strike first

indicators.note: about means going round, so copper-plus-head is placed around the next letter

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
pate is an old word for the head

indicators.note: first here picks the opening letter of the word strike

explanation.surface: A warning about a venomous snake that is ready to lash out before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copperhead' looks like the venomous snake but splits in two; 'about' wraps that pair round S, the first letter of 'strike'; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuspate describes something with a cusp, that is, tapering to a sharp tip.

clue.text: Hollow business decoration.

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on an honour given for commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: A COMBE is a short valley in southern England; an MBE is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A combe is a short valley or deep hollow in a hillside.

clue.text: Plant. needing little water yet, yielding weighty harvest

parts.note: a stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds
a crop is what is harvested

explanation.surface: A drought-tolerant plant that still gives a heavy yield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yet yielding' is link material; a STONE is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonecrop, or sedum, is a succulent that thrives in dry, rocky places.

clue.text: Yards or square measures

definitions.meaning: sunken courts in front of basements

explanation.surface: A question of whether lengths or surfaces are meant.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage an area is the sunken yard in front of a basement.
explanation.definitionFit: Basement courtyards are called areas in Britain, and an area is a surface measured in square units.

clue.text: Movement in net rate leads to appeal

indicators.note: movement in the letters means they shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Shifts in the net interest rate prompt a plea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement in' signals the anagram of NET RATE; 'leads to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to beg or plead earnestly.

clue.text: Right -.breathe out and relax

parts.note: to emit is to give out, as breath is given out

explanation.surface: Instructions for calming down: exhale and unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit is to slacken or ease off, as a fever or effort lessens.

clue.text: Dreamy but not solemn composition

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A piece of music that is reverie-like rather than grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' signals the anagram of NOT SOLEMN.
explanation.definitionFit: Somnolent means drowsy, on the edge of sleep, close to dreamy.

clue.text: Has note to mail first, so must be quick

indicators.note: first tells us the mail word comes before the other pieces

parts.note: to post a letter is to mail it
taken as written
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Advice to send a letter off urgently before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts POST ahead of HAS and TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste means with all possible speed, so very swift.

clue.text: Follow directions and engage in litigation

parts.note: E is east, a compass direction
N is north, another compass direction
to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: Advice to obey instructions and then go to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after as a result, synonymous with succeeding.

clue.text: Order a little English — Portuguese dictionary

indicators.note: a little of the phrase means only a short run of its letters is taken

explanation.surface: Asking for a small bilingual English to Portuguese reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English' is only part of the surface; the run sits across 'PortuguesE DICTionary'.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree or command.

clue.text: Walk about certain to be much appreciated

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the walking word goes round the other

parts.note: to tread is to walk
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A stroll around that is sure to be welcomed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something treasured is cherished and highly valued.

clue.text: Noah kept spinners busy!

parts.note: Noah built a famous boat, so he was a boat-builder; and the eighteenth-century inventor of that name made spinning machinery that kept textile spinners employed

explanation.surface: A biblical patriarch running a spinning mill.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Arkwright invented the water frame for spinning cotton; a 'wright' is a builder, and Noah built an ark.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah was a builder of an ark, and the industrialist Richard of that name mechanised spinning.

clue.text: He makes a snatch and 'turns in smoked fish

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the fish

parts.note: a kipper is a smoked herring

indicators.note: turns means the word and is read backwards

explanation.surface: A thief grabs something and then changes into a herring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' makes DNA from AND, which goes 'in' KIPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: An abductor seizes a person, often for ransom.

clue.text: Organising some great fuel store

indicators.note: organising means putting the letters into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Arranging a fine depot for fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organising' signals the anagram of SOME GREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasometer is a large tank holding town gas for supply.

clue.text: Called without once, getting cocky

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: cited means called, as a witness is summoned to court
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone summoned, without ever going even once, turns arrogant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, so the calling word wraps round 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceited means vain and self-satisfied, much like arrogant.

clue.text: P for Paris, for instance

parts.note: the opening letter of a city name is an upper-case letter, and the French city is the seat of government

explanation.surface: A phonetic spelling of a city's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses work: P is an upper-case letter, and Paris is a nation's chief city.
explanation.definitionFit: An upper-case letter and a seat of government are both called by this word.

clue.text: Finished a cereal food

parts.note: something past is over and done with

explanation.surface: Someone has eaten up a bowl of breakfast cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is made from durum wheat, a cereal, so it is a cereal-based food.

clue.text: Place article in box, say

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
taken as written
box is a kind of tree, hence say

explanation.surface: Instructions to put an item into a container.
explanation.walkthrough: AINTREE is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National; 'box' is the shrub, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a racecourse near Liverpool, a location famous for steeplechasing.

clue.text: Newsmen in force?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether reporters are present in large numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Reporters as a body are the press, and to press is to push or compel.

clue.text: At one time craft upside down were spare

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: in a down clue upside down means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: art is craft or skill

explanation.surface: Boats that once capsized are now surplus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upside down' turns ART into TRA in this down entry; 'were' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional or surplus, beyond what is needed.

clue.text: Coloured people standing up for William

definitions.text: Coloured people standing up for William

parts.words: Coloured people standing up for William
parts.note: people of a particular hue who support King William III, Prince of Orange, the Protestant king

explanation.surface: Tinted figures rising in support of someone called William.
explanation.walkthrough: Orangemen are members of the Orange Order, a Protestant fraternity in Northern Ireland named for William of Orange.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orange Order's members honour William of Orange, and their name contains a colour.

clue.text: An article in gold is different

indicators.note: in means the article word sits inside the heraldic metal

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A grammatical article set in gold looks unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means not the same, distinct.

clue.text: Beastly food provided by Greek simpleton

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Unpleasant dinner served by a foolish Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' means food for beasts, not nasty food.
explanation.definitionFit: Grazing animals eat grass, so it is fodder for livestock.

clue.text: Instruction to rush it may be given quietly

indicators.note: suggests the letters can be handed out in another form, an anagram signal

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a hurried job might be handed over without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be given' signals rearranging TO RUSH IT into TUTORSHI, then P is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutorship is the office or work of a tutor, that is, teaching.

clue.text: Like the heartless Russian leader making a bloomer

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word the is taken away
a leader comes first, so take the opening letter of Russian

explanation.surface: Comparing someone to a cold Russian ruler who makes a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes H from THE, leaving TE; 'Russian leader' looks like a tsar but is just R.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a flowering plant, and the Michaelmas daisy is one such.

clue.text: Hero's love, with a sly look — about it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the look goes round the joining word

parts.note: a leer is a sly or lascivious look
and means with, joining things together

explanation.surface: A lover glances knowingly at something.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to his love Hero; 'Hero' is a name, not a brave person.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Greek legend the young man swam the Hellespont nightly to his lover, the priestess Hero.

clue.text: Note answer in book

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
to serve is to answer, as in something that will answer the purpose

explanation.surface: A reminder to jot down a reply inside a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: To book a table is to reserve it, arranging it in advance.
